title: Seconds in a Year
problem: Estimate the number of seconds in a non-leap year without a calculator, then compare with the exact value.

hints.text: Multiply days per year, hours per day, minutes per hour, and seconds per minute.
Use 365≈400 or remember that one day has 86,400 seconds; a good mental benchmark is about 3.15×10^7.

solution.setup: Preserve units while multiplying: 365 days × 24 hours/day × 60 minutes/hour × 60 seconds/minute.
solution.reasoning: A fast estimate is 365×24≈8,760 hours, then ×3,600≈31.5 million seconds. Exactly, 365×24×60×60=31,536,000.
solution.sanityCheck: A million seconds is about 11.6 days, so a year should contain a little over 31 million seconds.

keyInsight: Dimensional decomposition makes large quantities manageable and exposes unit errors.
recognitionCues: A large unfamiliar count can be decomposed into familiar rates with units that cancel.
commonMistakes: Losing a factor of 60 while converting hours to seconds.
followUps: Estimate how many heartbeats occur in an 80-year lifetime.
